title: Democrats take the House and Senate
caption: The day after the midterms, CBS News projected that Democrats had won majorities in both the House and the Senate. Speaker Mike Johnson said he would not stay on as Republican leader, and Hakeem Jeffries announced his bid for speaker. The new Congress takes over in January, ending unified Republican control in Washington for President Trump's final two years.

stories.name: Democrats win control of the House and Senate
facts: On Nov. 4, the day after the 2026 midterm elections, CBS News projected that Democrats had won majorities in both the House and the Senate; NBC News also reported Democrats taking both chambers.
Republican Sen. Ted Cruz said on his podcast, "We've lost the House, we've lost the Senate."
House Speaker Mike Johnson told his staff Wednesday morning he will not stay on as Republican leader in the new Congress; Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan announced bids for minority leader.

Hakeem Jeffries announced his candidacy for speaker in a letter to House Democrats; Democratic leaders laid out priorities including lowering costs, restoring ACA subsidies, reversing Medicaid cuts, undoing tariffs and ending the Iran war.
The new Congress begins in January; Mississippi's Senate race was still too close to call that evening.

artwork.alt: Poster-style illustration of the US Capitol's white marble east front, with its dome, central portico and House and Senate wings, glowing apricot in low dawn light. A towering stylized blue wave rises behind the building and curls over the dome, a symbol of the 'blue wave' rather than a real event. In the foreground a small TV crew films a reporter and three passers-by walk toward the steps, casting long shadows. Represents Democrats winning control of both chambers of Congress.
